parts.description: A collection of nine cylindrical bottles and jars made from diverse materials including glass, ceramic, and metal, each fitted with unique closures such as wood, cork, or metal screw-caps.
parts.reasoning: The objects are representative of typical household containers, approximately 20-25 cm in height and 6-8 cm in diameter. The dominant materials across the set are rigid, dense substances like glass and ceramic. Based on standard household bottles, an average empty mass of 0.45 kg is estimated, with a density typical of glass/ceramic (around 2500 kg/m³). The smooth external surfaces result in relatively low friction coefficients (0.3-0.4). Restitution is kept moderate (0.4) as glass and ceramic are stiff but brittle. For simulation in Isaac Sim, a convex_decomposition collider is recommended to accurately represent the cylindrical body and the neck/lid variations, ensuring stable resting states and realistic rolling behavior. Continuous Collision Detection (CCD) is enabled to prevent tunneling if the bottles are knocked over or fall at high speeds.
